name: Illinois

ttd.rateText: Two-thirds of the employee's average weekly wage (820 ILCS 305/8(b)), up to the IWCC maximum, which is reset every January 15 and July 15 from the statewide average weekly wage published by IDES (Section 8(b)6).
ttd.minText: The minimum is the employee's average weekly wage or the IWCC rate, whichever is lower: $400.00 with no spouse/children, $460.00 (1), $520.00 (2), $580.00 (3), $600.00 (4 or more), for July 15, 2026 - January 14, 2027.

waiting.text: No TTD is paid for the first 3 working days unless the incapacity extends beyond 14 days, in which case compensation is paid from the start (820 ILCS 305/8(b)).

ttdDuration.text: TTD is paid for the duration of temporary total incapacity, with no fixed week cap (820 ILCS 305/8(b)).

ppd.text: Permanent partial disability (other than amputation or enucleation) has its own maximum, updated each July 1: $1,084.66 for July 1, 2025 - June 30, 2026; PPD minimums equal the TTD minimums. Wage-differential awards under Section 8(d)1 are capped at the SAWW. Amputation/enucleation PPD uses the higher death/PTD maximum ($2,045.63 from July 15, 2026). Schedule of weeks per member in 820 ILCS 305/8(e).

facts.text: Illinois resets its maximum and minimum rates twice a year, on January 15 and July 15, from the statewide average weekly wage published by the Illinois Department of Employment Security (Section 8(b)6).
The TTD minimum rises with the number of dependents (from $400.00 with none to $600.00 with four or more) and is tied to the state minimum wage, which reached $15.00/hour on January 1, 2025.
Death benefits are paid for 25 years or $500,000, whichever is greater, and death and PTD recipients may get cost-of-living adjustments through the Rate Adjustment Fund.
If only TTD, PPD or medical expenses are disputed, parties may agree to voluntary binding arbitration before an arbitrator recommended by the Workers' Compensation Advisory Board (Section 19(p)).
